tooltip.q1.welcome: January 2017. You have $10,000, a garage and a 12¢ power bill. Bitcoin is $1,000. Ethereum is $8. Nobody you know cares.
tooltip.q1.buy_rig: A GPU rig mines Ether. It costs about $2,000 and starts earning next quarter. Check power cost against revenue before you buy.
tooltip.q1.bandwidth: Bandwidth is your attention. You get 3 per quarter. Buying machines is free; scouting, pitching and hiring cost Bandwidth.
tooltip.q1.hodl: Each quarter, choose how much of what you mine to sell. Selling pays the bills. Holding bets on the price.
tooltip.act2.projects: Every megawatt you own can be converted into a project: pick a use, then fill its three slots: Power, Tenant, Capital. Nothing builds until all three are filled (a pilot cluster has no tenant slot).
tooltip.act2.mw_uses: A megawatt is always doing exactly one thing: mining, hosting someone else's machines, leased to an AI tenant (shell), running your own GPUs (full stack), or sitting idle and costing you money.
tooltip.act2.credit_rating: Your credit rating (CCC to BBB) is new: Act I had no such meter. It's set by your leverage and the quality of your signed contracts, and it decides what any new lender will charge you.
tooltip.act2.backlog: Signing a long contract is worth more than the cash it brings in this quarter: it adds to your contracted backlog, which the market rewards even before the money arrives. A hyperscaler's signature counts for more than an AI lab's.
tooltip.act2.take_or_pay: A signed tenant sets a ready-by date. Miss it by a quarter and you pay a penalty. Miss it by two, and they might just leave.
tooltip.act2.regions: Every site now carries a region tag. It's not just flavor: power price, grid queue time, and how fast the neighbors turn on you all depend on where you build.
tooltip.act2.pilot_cluster: Not ready for a big tenant? A pilot cluster is the smallest way into AI: half a megawatt to two megawatts of your own GPUs, rented out at the going cloud price, with no tenant to win first. Expect them to sit idle some of the time (about 30% at first); you get better at it as you learn.
tooltip.q1.live: The quarter plays out week by week. Prices move. If a week's revenue falls below power cost, your rigs switch off automatically.
tooltip.q1.report: Your quarter report: revenue, cost per coin, cash and rank. Cash below zero at quarter end means forced machine sales.
glossary.hashrate: How much guessing power a machine or network has. More hashrate means a bigger share of the rewards.
glossary.hashprice: What one unit of hashrate earns per day, in dollars: the single best measure of a miner's revenue. All else equal, it halves at each halving. When it falls below what a machine's power costs, that machine loses money.
glossary.difficulty: How hard the network makes the mining puzzle. It rises as more machines join, so each machine finds fewer coins even when nothing else changes. In the early years it barely moved; from 2013 it could double in a few months.
glossary.halving: Every four years the bitcoin block reward is cut in half. Revenue per machine roughly halves overnight.
glossary.hodl: Holding the coins you mine instead of selling them. Great in bull markets, dangerous when bills are due: coins you hold can't pay the power bill until you sell them.
glossary.asic: A chip built for one job. Bitcoin ASICs are far more efficient than GPUs but can do nothing else.
glossary.gpu: A graphics card. Mined Ether until September 2022; resellable to gamers and, later, AI labs.
glossary.mhs: Megahashes per second: millions of guesses per second. Used for Ether mining with GPUs.
glossary.ths: Terahashes per second: trillions of guesses per second. Used for bitcoin ASICs.
glossary.ehs: Exahashes per second: a million TH/s. Used to measure whole networks and large miners.
glossary.jth: Joules per terahash. Lower is better: less electricity for the same hashing.
glossary.pue: Power usage effectiveness: total site power divided by machine power. 1.1 means 10% goes to fans and losses.
glossary.curtailment: Switching off on request when the grid is stressed. Utilities pay for it, or you resell your power.
glossary.demand_response: Programmes that pay large power users to reduce load at peak times.
glossary.ltv: Loan-to-value: the loan divided by the collateral's value. If it climbs too high, the lender acts.
glossary.margin_call: The lender's demand for more collateral after prices fall. Ignore it and they sell your coins.
glossary.liquidation: The lender selling your collateral to repay the loan, usually at the worst moment.
glossary.spac: A listed shell company that merges with a private one, taking it public faster than an IPO.
glossary.ipo: Initial public offering: selling shares on a stock exchange for the first time.
glossary.ebitda: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation: roughly, operating cash profit.
glossary.ev_ebitda: Enterprise value divided by EBITDA. The market's multiple on your earnings; it swings wildly by era.
glossary.capex: Capital expenditure: money spent on things that last, like machines, transformers and buildings.
glossary.opex: Operating expenses: the recurring costs, above all electricity, rent and salaries.
glossary.cost_per_coin: All-in cost to mine one bitcoin or ether. Below the price, you profit; above it, you pay to mine.
glossary.hosting: Running other people's machines in your site for a fee per kWh.
glossary.merge: Ethereum's switch to proof-of-stake on 15 September 2022. GPU mining of Ether ended that day.
glossary.dilution: Your ownership share shrinking when you sell new shares to investors.
glossary.bandwidth: Your time and attention as founder each quarter. Strategic actions cost it, and unused Bandwidth is lost when the quarter ends. Hires and bigger sites give you more.
glossary.heat: How annoyed a site's neighbours, council and utility are, from 0 to 100. Complaints start at 30, a power rate hike comes at 50, no new machines at 70 and a shutdown at 90.
glossary.solo_pool: Solo: you keep a whole block when you find one, which may be never. Pool: many miners share every block, so you get a small, steady cut, minus a fee.
glossary.patience: How much more of the household load your parents will put up with. Over the limit it drops every quarter; at zero you must choose.
glossary.wallet_exchange: Only coins on an exchange can be sold, but an exchange can be hacked or fail. Coins in your own wallet are safe from that.
glossary.selling_limit: Early markets are thin: you can sell only so much each quarter, and big sales push the price down.
glossary.treasury: Coins you've mined and kept instead of selling, at this week's price. Sell them when you need cash.
glossary.valuation: What the company would be worth now: its earnings times the era's multiple, plus cash and coins, minus debt. Investors price your rounds on it.
glossary.rating: How lenders grade your company, from CCC− to BBB. It sets your loan rates and limits, and moves with your debt against your earnings.
glossary.backlog: The rent your signed contracts still have to pay. Lenders count it as safe future income, weighted by how good each tenant's credit is.
glossary.leverage: Your debt divided by a year's operating profit (EBITDA). The higher it is, the lower your rating and the dearer your loans.
glossary.ddtl: A delayed-draw term loan secured on your GPUs: drawn as the cloud is built, repaid from the GPU contract's payments.
glossary.mw_uses: Every energized MW is mining, hosting, an AI shell, an AI cloud, being built, or idle. Idle MW still cost a quarter of their full power bill.
glossary.renewal_wall: How many MW of your contracts reach their end quarter each quarter. Each one becomes a renewal decision: the more due at once, the more your income depends on that quarter's market.
glossary.today_rate: What a comparable new contract would pay this quarter, for the same MW or GPUs. Far below your current rent means a renewal will likely reprice down.
glossary.reopener: Either side can reopen a lease's rent before its end, for a fee of half a quarter's rent. Tenants reopen when market rents have fallen well below theirs.
glossary.blend_extend: A tenant offers to extend the lease now at one blended rent: part today's rent, part the market's. You trade some rent today for years of certainty.
glossary.signals: Six 0–100 indicators with a trend arrow. Each reading is noisy; reading the market (1 Bandwidth) shows one indicator's true range this quarter.
glossary.density: A hall's kW per rack: low (Hopper), mid (Blackwell, Rubin) or top (Rubin Ultra). A GPU only fits a hall of its tier or denser.
glossary.political_capital: Goodwill with regulators and grid operators, 0–100. It fades 2 a quarter. Spend it on permits and queues; below 15, moratoriums come sooner.
glossary.covenant: Lenders' limit on debt ÷ company value. In breach: no new loans, half your operating cash repays debt, and two quarters to cure before forced sales.
glossary.standby: A credit line you arrange in advance for a fee and draw only when needed. It's drawn automatically before any forced sale.
glossary.nuclear_ppa: A 15-year power contract at a fixed price. Take-or-pay: you pay for 90% of the contracted power whether you use it or not.
glossary_short.hashprice: What a unit of hashrate earns per day, in dollars. It halves at each halving; below a machine's power cost, that machine loses money.
glossary_short.difficulty: How hard the network makes the mining puzzle. It rises as more machines join, so the same rig finds fewer coins.
glossary_short.hodl: Holding the coins you mine instead of selling them: great when prices rise, dangerous when bills are due.
glossary_short.bandwidth: Your time and attention as founder each quarter. Big actions cost it; hires and bigger sites bring more.
glossary_short.heat: How annoyed a site's neighbours, council and utility are (0–100). The higher it climbs, the more it costs you.

event.gpu_shortage_2017.title: Graphics Cards: Sold Out
event.gpu_shortage_2017.body: Every shop has the same sign: no RX 580s, no ETA. A forum seller will ship six cards at 60% over list. Gamers are furious. Your spreadsheet is delighted.
event.gpu_shortage_2017.choice.markup: Pay the markup for one rig
event.gpu_shortage_2017.hint.markup: One Gen 1 rig now at 1.6× the new price; it earns from next quarter.
event.gpu_shortage_2017.hint.wait: No new GPU rigs next quarter.
event.gpu_shortage_2017.hint.used: One used Gen 1 rig now at the used price.
event.btc_peak_2017.title: Nineteen Thousand
event.btc_peak_2017.body: Bitcoin touches $19,000, a new record. Your barber asks about wallets. Your cousin wants to quit his job to mine.
event.btc_peak_2017.hint.sell_half: Sell half of your BTC and ETH at this week's prices.
event.btc_peak_2017.choice.buy_more: Buy more machines at today's prices
event.btc_peak_2017.hint.buy_more: Next Plan phase opens on the Buy dialog, with machines at a 10% premium (everyone else wants them too).
event.winter_bottom_2018.title: Capitulation
event.winter_bottom_2018.body: Network hashrate is falling for the first time in years. Farms are dumping S9s by the container. With ETH at $85, most garage rigs now lose money every night.
event.winter_bottom_2018.choice.shop: Go shopping in the fire sale
event.winter_bottom_2018.hint.shop: A distressed lot is guaranteed in next quarter's Plan phase.
event.winter_bottom_2018.hint.mothball: Every machine off until spring (the rest of this quarter and all of next): no power bill, rent ×0.3.
event.winter_bottom_2018.choice.sell_hal: Sell half the rigs while anyone still buys
event.winter_bottom_2018.hint.sell_half: Sell half of every batch now at the used price.
event.gpu_cloud_rumour_2019.title: The Other Use for GPUs
event.gpu_cloud_rumour_2019.body: An old contact says a small ETH farm in New Jersey is quietly renting its cards to render studios and AI researchers. 'Better margin than mining,' he claims. Nobody else seems interested.
event.covid_crash_2020.title: Black Thursday
event.covid_crash_2020.body: Markets everywhere are selling everything. Bitcoin drops 40% in a day. The next difficulty adjustment is two weeks away, and every S9 on the network is suddenly underwater.
event.covid_crash_2020.choice.sell_half: Sell half the treasury to protect cash
event.covid_crash_2020.hint.sell_half: Sell half of your BTC and ETH at this week's prices.
event.covid_crash_2020.hint.buy_cheap: Next Plan phase: used machines 30% cheaper, and it opens on the Buy dialog.
event.halving_2020.title: The Third Halving
event.halving_2020.body: Block 630,000. The reward drops from 12.5 to 6.25 BTC overnight. Anything less efficient than the new S19 is now a space heater with opinions.
event.halving_2020.choice.switch: Sell every S9 and move to S19 Pros
event.halving_2020.hint.switch: Sell every S9 now at the used price; next Plan phase opens on the Buy dialog.
event.halving_2020.choice.keep: Keep the S9s where power is cheapest
event.halving_2020.hint.keep: Keep the S9s running (they switch themselves off when they lose money).
event.halving_2020.hint.retire: Sell every S9 now at the used price.
event.uri_2021.title: Winter Storm Uri
event.uri_2021.body: Texas freezes. Grid prices hit the $9,000/MWh cap. The grid operator asks large loads to shut down. At your contract price, the power you are not using is worth more than the bitcoin you would mine.
event.spac_mania_2021.title: Everyone Wants a Miner
event.spac_mania_2021.body: Bankers call daily. Two blank-check companies want to merge with you at 'thirty times forward EBITDA'. Bitcoin makes a new all-time high. The window is open. Nobody knows for how long.
event.spac_mania_2021.hint.roadshow: The IPO / SPAC roadshow costs 2 Bandwidth instead of 3 for the rest of 2021.
event.spac_mania_2021.hint.private: Nothing changes; the IPO stays open until 2021Q4.
event.spac_mania_2021.body_news: Everyone is going public except you. Blank-check companies are merging with any miner that has 20 MW and real profits. Bitcoin makes a new all-time high. The IPO window is open until 2021Q4, if you can qualify.
event.spac_mania_2021.hint.ok: News only. The IPO needs a 20 MW site and $3M of quarterly EBITDA.
event.china_ban_2021.title: The Great Migration
event.china_ban_2021.body: China orders miners to shut down. Half the world's hashrate goes dark within weeks. Container ships full of S19s head for Texas and Kazakhstan. Every machine still running just got a much bigger slice of the rewards.
event.china_ban_2021.choice.buy_exiles: Buy exiled machines at a discount
event.china_ban_2021.hint.buy_exiles: Next Plan phase: used machines 25% cheaper, and it opens on the Buy dialog.
event.china_ban_2021.choice.rent_racks: Rent spare racks to an exiled miner
event.china_ban_2021.hint.rent_racks: $50K per spare MW (up to 10 MW), once.
event.luna_celsius_2022.title: Contagion
event.luna_celsius_2022.body: A $40B stablecoin melted in three days. Now a big crypto lender has 'paused withdrawals'. Every lender in the space wants its collateral back, today.
event.luna_celsius_2022.choice.repay: Repay crypto loans from the treasury
event.luna_celsius_2022.hint.repay: The lender sells enough of your pledged coins to repay the loan and returns the rest.
event.luna_celsius_2022.choice.sell_half: Sell half the treasury before it falls further
event.luna_celsius_2022.hint.sell_half: Sell half of your BTC and ETH at this week's prices.
event.luna_celsius_2022.hint.ride: For the rest of this quarter, margin calls come at 60% LTV and liquidation at 70%.
event.farm_fire.title: Smoke in the Rack
event.farm_fire.body: A PDU overheats at 3 a.m. The sprinklers work. So does the insurance, eventually.
event.farm_fire.hint.rebuild: Pay the larger of $20K or 5% of your fleet's used value; that site runs at 85% for 13 weeks.
event.farm_fire.hint.patch: Failures at that site ×1.5 for the rest of the quarter; neighbours' grievance +5.
event.landlord_eviction.title: The Building Is Sold
event.landlord_eviction.body: Your landlord has sold the building to a self-storage chain. You have one quarter to move, or to make the buyer an offer.
event.landlord_eviction.hint.move: Two quarters of rent to move; that site runs at 50% for 13 weeks.
event.landlord_eviction.hint.buy: Pay 12 quarters of rent once; no more rent at that site.
event.section301_tariff.title: Customs Hold
event.section301_tariff.body: Your new ASICs are sitting at Long Beach. Customs has reclassified them under the new China tariffs. Pay the duty or wait for a ruling.
event.section301_tariff.hint.pay: Pay 25% of what you spent on new ASICs this quarter; they arrive on time.
event.section301_tariff.hint.wait: Your undelivered new ASICs arrive a quarter later.
event.moratorium.title: Moratorium Vote
event.moratorium.body: The council votes 4–1 for an 18-month pause on new mining load. Existing machines may keep running. Your expansion may not.
event.moratorium.hint.lawyer: $80K. 40% chance: the moratorium is lifted at that site for 4 quarters, even above Heat 70.
event.moratorium.hint.accept: No machine purchases at that site while its Heat is 70 or more.
event.rig_theft.title: Missing Inventory
event.rig_theft.body: The side door was open. Some of your machines are gone. The police officer asks what a hashrate is.
event.rig_theft.choice.security: Take the loss and install security
event.rig_theft.hint.security: A quarter of the units there are gone (1 to 4), and $8K for locks and cameras.
event.rig_theft.hint.loss: A quarter of the units there are gone (1 to 4).
event.used_rig_scam.title: Too Good to Be True
event.used_rig_scam.body: A seller offers S19s at half the market price. Bank transfer only, 'shipping from Shenzhen'.
event.used_rig_scam.hint.deposit: Send 30% of this quarter's used purchases as a deposit. 20% chance it's real: used machines half price next Plan phase.
event.utility_rate_hike.title: New Rate Class
event.utility_rate_hike.body: The utility creates a 'high-density load' tariff. It applies to exactly one kind of customer.
event.utility_rate_hike.hint.accept: Power at that site ×1.3 until its next contract renewal.
event.utility_rate_hike.hint.fight: Power at that site ×1.1 until its next renewal, and 2 Bandwidth less next quarter.
event.heat_wave.title: Heat Dome
event.heat_wave.body: Forty-two degrees outside, forty-eight inside. Hashboards are dropping one after another.
event.heat_wave.hint.underclock: Sites of 1 MW and more run at 85% for the rest of the quarter.
event.heat_wave.hint.run_hot: Failures ×2 at sites of 1 MW and more for the rest of the quarter (and failure waves twice as likely).
event.heat_wave.hint.chillers: $40K × your MW at those sites ÷ 5 (at least $40K).
event.friend_wants_money.title: A Friend Calls
event.friend_wants_money.body: One of your early backers is buying a flat. They'd like their $15,000 back. They're sure you understand.
event.tax_surprise.title: Mined Coins Are Income
event.tax_surprise.body: Your accountant explains that every coin you mined was taxable income on the day you mined it. Including the ones now worth half that.
event.tax_surprise.hint.pay: 20% of your last 4 quarters' EBITDA (if positive), now.
event.tax_surprise.hint.plan: 6% now and 6% at the start of each of the next 3 quarters (24% in all).
p0.intro: January 2009. You're a tech student with a gaming PC, a couple thousand dollars saved, and a part-time job that covers pizza and rent-free living at home. A program a stranger posted on a mailing list just started running on your machine — something about decentralized digital cash, signed by a name nobody can place. It isn't worth anything. There's no market for it, no exchange, no price. You leave it running anyway, because it costs you nothing but electricity your parents are already paying for, and because you're curious. Eight years from now, in a garage, this decision will still be the one that matters most.

p0.news.2010Q2.0: A Florida programmer pays 10,000 coins for two pizzas
p0.news.2010Q3.0: A small Japanese trading card site relaunches as a bitcoin exchange
p0.news.2010Q3.1: A software bug briefly creates 184 billion coins before the network patches itself
p0.news.2010Q4.0: The first pooled mining service opens; miners can now split rewards instead of gambling alone
p0.news.2011Q1.0: Bitcoin reaches parity with the US dollar for the first time
p0.news.2011Q2.0: Bitcoin touches $31 before a hacked exchange account crashes the price toward a cent
p0.news.2011Q4.0: Bitcoin bottoms near $2, down more than 90% from June's high
p0.news.2012Q4.0: The first halving cuts the block reward from 50 to 25 coins
p0.news.2013Q1.0: The first purpose-built mining chips start taking pre-orders
p0.news.2013Q2.0: A Cyprus banking crisis is credited with a bitcoin rally past $260
p0.news.2013Q4.0: Federal agents shut down the Silk Road marketplace and seize tens of thousands of coins
p0.news.2013Q4.1: Bitcoin crosses $1,000 for the first time
p0.news.2013Q4.2: China bars its financial institutions from bitcoin business; the price drops hard
p0.news.2014Q1.0: The exchange that dominates bitcoin trading halts withdrawals, then goes offline, then files for bankruptcy
p0.news.2015Q3.0: A new blockchain, Ethereum, launches with its own coin and its own miners
p0.news.2016Q3.0: A smart contract holding millions of the new coin is drained overnight
p0.news.2016Q3.1: The second halving cuts bitcoin's block reward from 25 to 12.5 coins
p0.news.2016Q3.2: A newer, more efficient mining machine goes on sale at a steep launch price
p0.news.2016Q3.3: Another exchange loses roughly 120,000 coins to hackers
p0.news.2016Q4.0: Eight years in, you're carrying everything you built into a real operation
p0.chapter_title.hodler_lost_gox: The One Who Trusted the Exchange
p0.chapter_title.lost_wallet: The One Who Never Backed Up
p0.event.genesis_block.title: Chancellor on Brink of Second Bailout
p0.event.genesis_block.body: A new program starts on your PC. Block zero carries a headline clipped from that morning's Times: banks, again, need saving. Nobody is paying you anything for this. There is nothing to sell it for yet.
p0.event.first_exchange_rate.title: A Price, of Sorts
p0.event.first_exchange_rate.body: A forum post proposes a rate: 1,309.03 coins to the dollar, worked out from the electricity it costs to mine one. It's not a market — nobody's actually trading at that number — but for the first time, there's a number.
p0.event.first_exchange_rate.choice.note: Note the number and keep mining
p0.event.first_exchange_rate.choice.mess: Message the poster to try a trade
p0.event.pizza_day.title: Two Pizzas
p0.event.pizza_day.body: Someone on the forum paid ten thousand coins for two pizzas. People are calling it the first real-world trade. You have your own offer sitting in your inbox, for a lot less than that per coin.
p0.event.mtgox_opens.title: A Real Exchange
p0.event.mtgox_opens.body: A Japanese site that used to trade Magic: The Gathering cards has pivoted to bitcoin. It has an order book, real volume, and a price that moves by the hour. Cards are also newly worth mining with — a decent GPU is many times faster than your CPU.
p0.event.mtgox_opens.choice.move_some: Move some coins to the exchange
p0.event.mtgox_opens.choice.keep_wallet: Keep everything in your own wallet for now
p0.event.mtgox_opens.choice.buy_gpu: Buy a gaming GPU (if you can afford one)
p0.event.value_overflow_bug.title: 184.467 Billion Coins
p0.event.value_overflow_bug.body: A bug let someone create 184 billion coins out of nothing in one transaction. The network patches itself within hours; a stricter chain overtakes the bad one the next day. Nothing you own is affected — it's just a reminder this is still very new software.
p0.event.bubble_and_hack_2011.title: Thirty-One Dollars, Then One Cent
p0.event.bubble_and_hack_2011.body: The price touched $31 last week. Today, a compromised trading account crashed the displayed price toward a single cent before the exchange rolled the trades back. Everyone on the forum is arguing about whether their coins are actually safe anywhere.
p0.event.bubble_and_hack_2011.choice.sel: Sell a chunk of what's on the exchange while it still trades
p0.event.bubble_and_hack_2011.choice.wit: Move everything into your own wallet
p0.event.crash_bottom_2011.title: Two Dollars
p0.event.crash_bottom_2011.body: The price that touched $31 in June is now about $2. Half the forum has stopped posting. A new kind of board just started shipping — an FPGA, purpose-leaning hardware that mines for a fraction of a GPU's power draw, if you can flash the bitstream yourself.
p0.event.crash_bottom_2011.choice.take_b: Take a break from buying anything
p0.event.first_halving.title: Twenty-Five, Not Fifty
p0.event.first_halving.body: Block 210,000. The reward that's paid every block was cut in half overnight, exactly as the code always said it would be. Anyone still mining with a GPU alone is starting to lose the arithmetic.
p0.event.asic_preorders_open.title: Pay Now, Mine Later
p0.event.asic_preorders_open.body: Two small companies are taking deposits for purpose-built mining chips, promised to ship 'next quarter'. One shipped its first batch almost on time. Most of these startups do not. A forum thread is also organizing a group buy — chip in for half a unit, split the hashrate with someone you've never met, for half the risk.
p0.event.asic_preorders_open.choice.grou: Join a group buy (half a unit, half the price)
p0.event.asic_preorders_open.choice.skip: Skip pre-orders, wait for retail ASICs
p0.event.cyprus_rally.title: The Bank Won't Open
p0.event.cyprus_rally.body: Cyprus proposed taking a cut of ordinary bank deposits to fund a bailout. Bitcoin's price quadrupled in weeks, past $260, before sliding hard the same week it peaked. Financial press outside crypto is finally paying attention.
p0.event.cyprus_rally.choice.hold: Hold through the crash back down
p0.event.peak_and_silk_road.title: Eleven Hundred Dollars, and the Marketplace Is Gone
p0.event.peak_and_silk_road.body: Bitcoin crossed a thousand dollars last week, then went higher — on the same exchange that hacked itself two years ago. Two months ago the FBI shut down the internet's biggest drug marketplace and seized tens of thousands of coins from its operator. None of it has slowed the price down.
p0.event.peak_and_silk_road.choice.sell_: Sell most of the treasury near the top
p0.event.china_ban_2013.title: Beijing Says No
p0.event.china_ban_2013.body: China's central bank has barred financial institutions from touching bitcoin. The price, still near its all-time high, drops hard on the news. Individuals can apparently still hold and trade it — for now.
p0.event.china_ban_2013.choice.sell_some: Sell some of the treasury on the drop
p0.event.mtgox_collapse.title: The Exchange Goes Dark
p0.event.mtgox_collapse.body: Withdrawals stopped three days ago over a technical excuse nobody fully buys. In two weeks the site will go blank, and in three, it will file for bankruptcy. Roughly 850,000 coins — most of it customer money — are unaccounted for. Whatever you left on that exchange, you're about to find out if you'll ever see it again.
p0.event.mtgox_collapse.choice.withdraw: Try to withdraw everything right now
p0.event.mtgox_collapse.choice.accept: Accept the loss and move on
p0.event.eth_launch.title: A Second Chain
p0.event.eth_launch.body: A new network launched this summer with its own coin and its own miners. It's still worth only a few dollars, but the GPUs you already own can mine it, and its own difficulty hasn't caught up yet.
p0.event.eth_launch.choice.build_rig: Build a GPU rig for the new coin
p0.event.dao_hack_fork.title: The Fund That Emptied Itself
p0.event.dao_hack_fork.body: A smart contract holding a huge pool of the new coin was drained overnight — about 3.6 million coins, roughly a third of what it held. The network is arguing about whether to rewrite history to get it back. A month from now they will, and the chain will split in two.
p0.event.dao_hack_fork.choice.watch: Watch and keep mining either way
p0.event.dao_hack_fork.choice.sell_eth: Sell your ETH holdings until the dust settles
p0.event.second_halving_s9.title: Twelve and a Half
p0.event.second_halving_s9.body: Block 420,000: the reward halves again, from 25 to 12.5. A new machine just went on sale that's more efficient than anything before it — expensive at launch, the way they always are.
p0.event.second_halving_s9.choice.buy_s9: Buy an Antminer S9 at launch prices
p0.event.second_halving_s9.choice.wait: Wait for the price to come down
p0.event.bitfinex_hack_news.title: Another Exchange, Another Hack
p0.event.bitfinex_hack_news.body: A different exchange just lost about 120,000 coins to a hack. The price drops sharply on the news, then starts to recover within days. You check which exchange you're using.
p0.event.bitfinex_hack_news.choice.withd: Move everything to your own wallet
p0.event.handover.title: Into the Garage
p0.event.handover.body: Whatever you built over the last eight years — the machines, the sites, the coins you kept and the ones you lost — comes with you now. It's 2017. You're doing this full-time.
p0.event.power_bill.title: The Electric Bill
p0.event.power_bill.body: Your mother puts the bill on the kitchen table and doesn't say anything. She doesn't have to.
p0.event.power_bill.choice.say_nothing: Say nothing and turn a rig off for a week
p0.event.pc_overheats.title: Too Hot to Touch
p0.event.pc_overheats.body: The case is hot enough to worry about. The fan sounds like it's dying because it is.
p0.event.friend_wants_coins.title: A Friend Asks
p0.event.friend_wants_coins.body: A friend heard you've got some of these internet coins and wants in, cash in hand, whatever the going rate is.
p0.event.friend_wants_coins.choice.decli: Tell them to buy their own
p0.event.dead_hard_drive.title: The Drive Won't Spin Up
p0.event.dead_hard_drive.body: The drive with your wallet on it just clicks instead of spinning. This is the moment a backup would have mattered.
p0.event.dead_hard_drive.choice.recovery: Roll the dice on data recovery
p0.event.job_offer.title: A Real Job Offer
p0.event.job_offer.body: A local shop wants you part-time, more hours than you have free. It pays better than what you're making now, if you can spare the time.
p0.event.conference_invitation.title: A Conference Invitation
p0.event.conference_invitation.body: There's a bitcoin conference this spring, real speakers, real vendors. It's not cheap to get to.
p0.event.household.title: Your Parents Have Had Enough
p0.event.household.body: The house is hot, the bill is huge, and the noise never stops. Either you move out, or the rigs at home run at half-strength this quarter.
